fix: the magnitude of the honors that had been bestowed on Antigonus and himself by the Achaeans
reason: αὐτοῖς = the Macedonian kings, honored by the Achaeans; English made the Achaeans honor themselves. Kept original wording otherwise.

fix: and stakes having these [...] are chosen [...] not alternately
reason: Two lacunae around λαμβάνονται; 'on one side only' is supplied text. Mark both gaps, drop the bracketed note.
Predicate lost after τοῖς διαγωνιζομένοις ***; 'locked in close combat' is invented. Use [...] only, no extra note.

fix: at first [...] halted, since the enemy held their pikes upright
reason: Lacuna after τὰς μὲν ἀρχὰς must be marked; causal genitive absolute is a fair reading, so 'since' stays.

fix: or because he did not wish, having driven Philip from power, to leave the Aetolians as masters of the Greeks
reason: εἴτ᾽ gives the second of two alternative motives (the first is in the lacuna), so 'nor' is wrong.

fix: [...] to prevent Antiochus from sailing along the coast
reason: The excerpt starts mid-sentence and its governing verb is lost; 'They tried' is supplied. Later 'they' is supported by ὑφορώμενοι.

fix: And they themselves at once pointed out which these places were, in their ingenious arguments with one another.
reason: τούτους = the places (τόπους); the speakers named them. 'Gave themselves away' is not the Greek. 'To their own cost' over-reads καθ᾽ αὑτῶν.

fix: there also arrived three of the ten commissioners
reason: The Greek names three: Lentulus, Terentius, Villius.
